open_obligations: Note the different tasks: chess and NLP versus harmlessness preference alignment.
Check whether Yang et al.'s gains are on the same metric (PGR) as Burns et al.'s.
Check consistency with Burns et al.'s finding of no improvement in reward modeling.
out.other_title: Bootstrapping through intermediate model sizes improves weak-to-strong PGR on chess
out.rationale: Burns et al. report bootstrapping through intermediate model sizes improves PGR on chess puzzles, with small or no gains on NLP and reward modeling. Yang et al. report that when the weak model supervises an intermediate model that then supervises Mistral-7B, weak-to-strong generalization improves and deception scores fall; Yang et al. use preference alignment on harmlessness, a setting where Burns et al. saw little bootstrapping benefit in reward modeling.
out.scope: proposed SUPPORTS: whether supervising through an intermediate model improves weak-to-strong generalization

text: The paper reports that when the weak model first supervises an intermediate model that then supervises Mistral-7B, bootstrapping improves weak-to-strong generalization (consistent with Burns et al.) and consistently lowers deception scores. The authors suggest some cases unknown to the weak model become known to the intermediate model, making deception harder there.
title: Bootstrapping through an intermediate model partly mitigates weak-to-strong deception
